details.description:
...The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande At Columbia Bridge affecting Webb County.

For the Rio Grande...including Columbia Bridge...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Columbia Bridge.

* WHEN...From Friday evening to Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 28 feet, or 8.5 meters, the flow reaches the height of
the left bank. Flow exceeds left bank near the gauge. Most of
customs and mall parking lots are inundated downstream in Laredo.
The lowest residences are threatened in Laredo and Nuevo Laredo.
Livestock, pumps, and equipment in the river channel are flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 9.5 feet (2.9 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 16.0 feet (4.9 meters).
- Forecast...The river is forecast to climb into caution stage by
Friday morning, with a continued rise through minor stage early
Saturday morning, and cresting near 29 ft early Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet (5.5 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.9
feet (8.8 meters) on 04/06/2004.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
details.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

title: Air Quality Alert
location: Lucas; Wood; Ottawa; Sandusky; Erie; Hancock; Seneca; Huron; Wyandot; Crawford; Richland; Ashland; Wayne; Stark; Marion; Morrow; Holmes; Knox

details.description:
The Ohio Environmental Protection Agency has issued an Air Quality
Advisory for the entire state of Ohio, until midnight EDT Friday
night.

Smoke from Canadian wildfires will adversely impact air quality
through Friday. The Ohio Environmental Protection Agency expects the
Air Quality Index to be in the 'Unhealthy' range. Hourly concentrations
at times may reach the 'Very Unhealthy' to 'Hazardous' categories.

It is recommended, when possible, to avoid strenuous outdoor
activities, especially those with heart disease and respiratory
conditions like asthma. Watch for symptoms including wheezing,
coughing, chest tightness, dizziness, or burning in the nose,
throat, and eyes.

For additional information, please visit the Ohio Environmental
Protection Agency's website at epa.ohio.gov.

The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has issued a
Code PURPLE Air Quality Alert for Erie and Crawford Counties. The
advisory is until midnight EDT Friday night.

Wildfire smoke from northern Minnesota and south central Canada will
continue to result in unhealthy air quality through Friday.

All Pennsylvania residents should limit time outdoors, especially
vulnerable populations, including small children, the elderly, and
those with respiratory ailments.

For more information on ground-level ozone and fine particles, visit
www.airnow.gov, and www.aqpartners.state.pa.us.

details.description:
* WHAT...For the Heat Advisory, hot conditions with afternoon
temperatures of 90 to 96 degrees. This will pose a moderate risk
of heat-related illness. For the Wind Advisory, west winds 20 to
30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph expected.

* WHERE...Lower Columbia Basin of Oregon.

* WHEN...For the Heat Advisory, until 9 PM PDT this evening. For the
Wind Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to 1 AM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
Patchy blowing dust may locally reduce visibilities. Hot
temperatures may cause heat illnesses.
details.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible.
To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

For sheltering information and other human services in your area,
dial 2 1 1 during business hours or visit 211info.org for Oregon or
wa211.org for Washington anytime.

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an

details.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Cottonwood burn scar in...
Eastern Beaver County in southern Utah...

* Until 400 PM MDT.

* At 206 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Cottonwood Burn Scar. Between 0.4 and 0.7
inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow
moving through the Beaver River. The debris flow can consist of
rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding in and around the Cottonwood
Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around
the Cottonwood Burn Scar...specifically in the Beaver
River downstream through the Grove Area in Beaver City

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beaver...especially the Grove Area
details.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and
ditches in the Cottonwood Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be
anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in
places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
